problems.problem: Rule 6. The key stops at Besant’s ‘to slay mankind’ and leaves out the next sentence, ‘Not one of all these warriors...’. Rāmānuja’s commentary on 11.32 (Govindacharya 1898, in the packet) limits the slaying to ‘this world of kings’, meaning those in Dhritarashtra’s faction and the warriors ‘ranged in opposition to thee’, whom the Lord destroys by his own fiat without waiting for Arjuna’s help. The sentence carries this limit only as ‘each king’s life-span’. With no side named, a reader of this key at six in the morning can take ‘each king’ as every king, or all mankind, so the limit Rāmānuja sets on the key verse’s line is not stated.
problems.fix: Keep the plain sense and the etymology, and name whose reckoning it is in Rāmānuja’s words: ‘...; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 11.32, takes Time from a root meaning to count: the one who reckons when the life-span of each king ranged against Arjuna runs out.’ The sentence stays under 45 words. The evidence already quoted from the packet supports it (‘Dhritarashtra ... and similarly of other royal dignitaries’; ‘warriors ranged in opposition to thee shall meet ruin’). Add the second phrase to the evidence words.
